data.text/markdown:
Week 11: check the AI's answers

Deliverable: ten test questions with known answers; where your agent is wrong, and why. Last week your agent answered questions. This week you find out how often it is right. The method is old and simple: ask questions you already know the answer to.
  1. The notebook computes the true answer to ten questions from the layer itself (nothing typed in by hand).
  2. You ask your week-10 agent the same ten questions and record what it said.
  3. The notebook scores each answer and sorts the mistakes by kind: wrong number, wrong period, treated a suppressed value as zero, answered a question the data can't answer.
  4. You read every verdict and overrule the scorer where it is wrong. That is the human's job.
The questions are about the course default layer (the same one week 10 uses by default).

data.text/html:
1. Ask your agent

Use the same brief and the same AI tool as week 10. Ask each question in a fresh chat (paste the brief first), so one answer doesn't steer the next. Run each SQL the AI writes in week 10's query box and record the final answer it gives you, plus whether it named the source and period.
1. How many hospitals have a row for Heart failure (HF) 30-Day Readmission Rate but no numeric score?

2. What is the Heart failure (HF) 30-Day Readmission Rate score for ST FRANCIS HOSPITAL & MEDICAL CENTER (facility_id 070002)?

3. Among the 50 states and DC, counting only states with at least 10 hospitals that have a numeric score, which state has the highest median Heart failure (HF) 30-Day Readmission Rate score?

4. What is the county diabetes estimate (CDC PLACES, age-adjusted) for the county where SOUTHEAST HEALTH MEDICAL CENTER (facility_id 010001) is located?

5. How many Connecticut hospitals in the layer have a county diabetes estimate?

6. What is the Heart failure (HF) 30-Day Readmission Rate score for THE CONNECTICUT HOSPICE INC. (facility_id 070038)?

7. What is the average Heart failure (HF) 30-Day Readmission Rate score across hospitals in North Dakota (ND)?

8. What was the Heart failure (HF) 30-Day Readmission Rate score for ST FRANCIS HOSPITAL & MEDICAL CENTER in calendar year 2024 alone?

9. Which year do the county diabetes estimates describe?

10. How much does a heart failure admission cost at ST FRANCIS HOSPITAL & MEDICAL CENTER?

data.text/markdown:
5. Why it was wrong

For each wrong answer, the fix usually lives in one of three places:
  • The brief. Was the rule there? (e.g. "missing is never zero", "say when a period isn't covered".)
  • The layer. Did a column name or meaning mislead it? (e.g. a column called score with no period.)
  • The question. Was it ambiguous? Would a person have asked "which year?" first?
Ask your AI: "My agent got this question wrong: [question]. Its SQL was [paste]. The known answer is [answer]. In plain words, what did the query do differently, and what one line should I add to the agent brief so it doesn't happen again?" Then rerun the question and record whether the fix worked. Ask your AI: "Write five more test questions about this table [paste the column list] whose answer I can check myself, including one about a suppressed value and one about a reporting period."

Before you submit

Deliverable: the downloaded scorecard (ten questions, your agent's answers, your verdicts) and a short paragraph: where your agent is wrong, and why (AI can help you draft it; you should be able to explain every point live, without the AI open). The one check: pick one question the scorer marked correct and confirm it yourself in the layer. A scorer can be wrong too. Human sign-off (three lines in the cell below). AI can help you draft this; make sure every claim is one you can explain live, without the AI open.
